source_name: T.C. Ziraat Bankası — İhale Portalı (tender portal)
why_relevant: Dedicated tender portal of the Turkish state-owned parent of ZIRAAT Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica. Unlike the Austrian/Hungarian/Slovenian parents, Ziraat operates a named, public-facing tender channel — the single most promising parent-level tender feed in this cell. Fetch returned only the page title, so tender-category coverage (whether IT/payments appear alongside the well-documented real-estate auctions) is unconfirmed.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Uzbekistan — İhaleler ve duyurular (foreign-subsidiary tender page template)
why_relevant: Proof that Ziraat foreign subsidiaries do publish their own tender/announcement pages under a shared template. Strong hypothesis that ZIRAAT Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica operates an equivalent /ihaleler or /tenderi page; this page gives the URL pattern and Turkish heading vocabulary to probe for it.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (Central Bank of Montenegro bank register)
why_relevant: Authoritative local register that establishes, per bank, the exact legal name and the foreign parent group — the ground truth for building the parent-to-subsidiary map this cell depends on (entries observed for CKB 'member of OTP Group', NLB Banka AD Podgorica, ERSTE Bank AD Podgorica, and NLB Crna Gora DOO among receivables-purchase companies). Ownership changes here are the trigger to re-point group-level monitoring.

source_name: EBA — DORA Register of Information / ICT third-party oversight
source_subtype: supranational regulator / ICT third-party register regime
why_relevant: Since 17 Jan 2025 EU financial entities must maintain a Register of Information on every ICT third-party contractual arrangement; competent authorities reported these to the ESAs by 30 Apr 2025, feeding the designation of critical ICT third-party providers. For Erste, NLB and Addiko this is a group-level, EU-supervised inventory of exactly the vendors that serve the Montenegrin subsidiary. The registers themselves are supervisory, not public, but the published designation lists and the EBA RoI reporting FAQs reveal taxonomy, scope and the named critical providers. OTP's Montenegrin subsidiary sits outside the EU perimeter, so coverage is partial.

source_name: beszerzes.hu — Hungarian procurement trade press (OTP tag)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language procurement trade publication with a dedicated OTP tag and supplier-qualification coverage. Trade press is often the only place where a parent bank's sourcing programme, category strategy or e-procurement rollout is described in operational detail before it appears in any formal notice.

source_name: Erste Group — International Desk: Montenegro country page
why_relevant: Group-maintained page describing the Montenegrin operation from Vienna's perspective (Erste present in ME since July 2009, 15 branches). Confirms group-level ownership of the Montenegro narrative and provides the group-side contact structure through which a vendor engagement for ME would be routed.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H, company of Erste Group Bank
why_relevant: Reveals the operating profile of Erste's central procurement entity: ~11-50 employees, HQ Vienna with own subsidiaries in CZ, HU, SK, RO and HR, three service lines (Sourcing for high-value strategic categories, Tactical Purchasing, Order Management), standardized supplier onboarding on a Supplier Code of Conduct, CIPS Ethics Mark. Category ownership and named sourcing managers are the practical route to identifying who decides Montenegrin payments spend.

source_name: Printec Montenegro (country page, Printec Group site)
why_relevant: Printec Montenegro d.o.o. (present in Montenegro since 2014) is a leading transaction-automation vendor to Montenegrin banks (ATM/kiosk, ATM software, cash management). The country page and its news items are the vendor-side record of local bank deployments that buyers rarely announce.

source_name: Printec Group Resources / case studies library
why_relevant: Central library of Printec case studies and success stories across 17 CEE/SEE countries; named-bank case studies (e.g. the publicly posted BPB Kosovo ATM fleet renewal) show the format in which Montenegrin bank wins would also surface. Pointer to further bank actors and solution categories.

source_name: Printec Group social channels (Facebook/LinkedIn) — customer win posts
why_relevant: Observed a Printec Facebook post explicitly naming a bank customer and the scope of an ATM-fleet renewal (BPB, Kosovo). Vendor social channels frequently carry deal announcements that never reach the corporate newsroom — a cheap early-warning channel for Montenegrin wins.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — Group structure page
why_relevant: ASEE is the largest SEE banking/payments software vendor. The group-structure page lists local legal entities including E-Mon (Podgorica, Montenegro, 75%) — i.e. an identifiable local ASEE arm whose customers are Montenegrin banks/PSPs. Pointer for further entity- and customer-level searching (company registry, tender bidder lists).

source_name: MoneyGet Crna Gora (Asseco-operated ATM network, Montenegro)
why_relevant: MoneyGet is an Asseco-run independent ATM network operating in Montenegro (.me domain). A vendor/operator-side source that reveals ATM estate, locations, sponsoring banks and expansion — direct evidence of who supplies and operates self-service infrastructure locally.

source_name: Asseco mobile/e-banking apps for Montenegrin banks (Google Play listings)
why_relevant: App package IDs are an unfalsifiable vendor fingerprint: 'hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbcrnagora.me' proves Asseco supplies NLB Banka Podgorica's retail and corporate mobile banking. App-store metadata (publisher, package prefix, release history) is a systematic way to map digital-channel vendors to Montenegrin banks without any press release existing.

source_name: Halcom — retail banking / e-banking solution pages and references
why_relevant: Halcom claims Hal E-Bank was the first functional e-banking system in Montenegro; the vendor's solution/reference pages are the supplier-side record of Montenegrin bank e-banking and digital-certificate deployments.

source_name: Logate (Podgorica) — Montenegrin software integrator for banks and telcos
why_relevant: Logate (founded 2006, Podgorica) implements and maintains software systems for banks and telecom operators in Montenegro and the region. A domestic supplier whose reference/news pages are one of the few local-language records of bank IT contracts.

source_name: ČIKOM d.o.o. (Podgorica) — leading Montenegrin ICT integrator, company/LinkedIn page
why_relevant: ČIKOM is described as one of Montenegro's leading ICT companies and digital-transformation integrators (70+ specialists), publicly disclosing consortium wins and contract values (e.g. a €1.3m ex-VAT CGES telecom system in Dec 2023). Same disclosure habit applies to financial-sector infrastructure deals, making its channels a supplier-side award record.

source_name: Amplitudo d.o.o. (Podgorica) — software vendor, hosts public-sector portals
why_relevant: Amplitudo builds and hosts Montenegrin institutional systems (observed serving the EKIP regulator portal from an amplitudo.me subdomain — ekip-cr.amplitudo.me). Infrastructure fingerprints like this reveal supplier-buyer relationships even where no announcement exists; the same technique can be applied to bank/PSP web properties.

source_name: ICT Cortex (Montenegrin ICT cluster) — member directory by capability
why_relevant: Cluster directory enumerating Montenegrin ICT companies by capability category. Best single pointer for building the domestic supplier actor-map (who could bid on bank/public payment projects) before hunting their individual reference pages.

source_name: Monri Payments (member of Payten) — regional payment gateway/POS vendor
why_relevant: Monri (part of Payten/Asseco ecosystem) states it works with 20+ financial institutions in the EU plus Bosnia, Serbia and Montenegro, and Payten acts as its EFTPOS installation subcontractor. Vendor-side evidence of POS/e-commerce acquiring supply into Montenegrin banks.

source_name: Payten / Monri LinkedIn company channels
why_relevant: Payten and Monri announce new bank/merchant acquiring partnerships on LinkedIn well before (or instead of) formal press releases; relevant for POS, switch/processing and e-commerce gateway wins in Montenegro.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom (global + Europe press releases)
why_relevant: Scheme-side announcements name issuing/acquiring banks and processors when a new product launches in a market (e.g. Mastercard/NCR Atleos/ITCARD contactless-at-ATM). For Montenegro, scheme press releases are often the only public trace of an issuer's technology partner.

source_name: Businesswire / vendor newswire distribution (e.g. Ripple–CBCG agreement)
why_relevant: Concrete precedent that supplier-issued newswire releases are the public record of Montenegrin financial-sector engagements: Ripple announced its CBDC strategy/pilot agreement with the Central Bank of Montenegro via Businesswire. Newswire archives are searchable for 'Montenegro' + vendor names.

source_name: ATM Marketplace (industry trade press for ATM/self-service vendors)
why_relevant: Trade outlet that reports ATM vendor deals, fleet renewals and vendor strategy (NCR Atleos / Diebold Nixdorf). Useful to catch supplier announcements for small markets that never reach mainstream press, and to track which vendors are active in SEE.
